stumbles.why: The reference is never named, so I can't tell what the colours were compared to. ΔE76 is jargon, and the sentence doesn't say what it implies. It also sits oddly next to the admission that the thing hasn't been tried on a phone.

stumbles.quote: thickness as density: thick film sinks toward the tilt, thin rises.
stumbles.why: It's terse and unclear whether this describes the simulation model or what I will see. The rule is stated but not explained.

stumbles.quote: It drains, goes black from the top, and pops.
stumbles.why: "It" is unclear, and so is why it goes black. A reader without soap-film physics won't know that black means a very thin film just before it bursts.

stumbles.quote: Not yet tried on a real phone.
stumbles.why: It contradicts the opening instruction to tilt your phone. The demo is meant for phones, but the author hasn't tested it on one. It's unclear whether it will work, and whether desktop is supported or WebGPU is needed.

point: A WebGPU soap-film simulation that you steer by tilting your phone. Thickness drives the flow, the film drains and pops, and the author hasn't tested it on a real phone.
